summary: Bunyiu Nanjio was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Sinology who studied at Oxford under Friedrich Max Müller and Arthur Anthony Macdonell. He served as Professor of Sanskrit at the University of Tokyo and President of Otani University.

Bunzaburo Matsumoto worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. After studying at the University of Tokyo, he held posts at the University of Tokyo (~1899–1906) and Kyoto University (1906–1929, attested as professeur in 1934).
Burkhard Quessel is a Tibetologist who studied at the University of Hamburg, where he was attested as a member in 1997. He served as a curator at the British Library (attested 2002–2012).

Burton Watson was a Sinologist and Japanologist who studied at Columbia University. He held posts at Kyoto University (~1952–1956), Stanford University (~1962–1963), and Columbia University, where he was a professor (~1961–1973).

Bötrül Dongak Tenpé Nyima worked in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied at Dzogchen Monastery under Thubten Nyendrak and Khenpo Genam, and later taught Khenpo Chökhyap, Khenpo Dazer, Jigme Phuntsok, and Tarthang Tulku.

C. D. Sebastian specializes in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He completed a PhD at Banaras Hindu University, had postdoctoral mentorship under Paul Williams and Gavin D'Costa, and became Professor of Indian Philosophy at IIT Bombay (attested 2016).

C. F. Lee studied at the University of Hong Kong (~1964–1970) and the University of Western Ontario (~1970–1972). He worked in Buddhist studies and other fields, serving as Pro-Vice-Chancellor of the University of Hong Kong (1994–2015).

C. Kunhan Raja was an Indologist who served as Head of the Department of Sanskrit at the University of Madras in 1927 and 1946. His students included K. Kunjunni Raja, Madhav Krishna Sharma, and H. G. Narahari.
C. R. Krishnamacharlu worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He completed his F. A. at Madras Christian College and received a university degree from Pachaiyappa's College.
C. S. Srinivasachariar worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He held posts as a professor at Pachaiyappa's College and Annamalai University (attested 1932–1933).
C. S. Sundaram was an Indologist who held posts at The Madras Sanskrit College and the University of Madras, where he became Reader in Sanskrit in 1951. He taught Tomy Augustine.

C. W. Huntington worked in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. He earned his PhD at the University of Michigan under Luis Oscar Gómez and Madhav M. Deshpande, and served as a professor at Hartwick College (~1993–2020).

Calambur Sivaramamurti was an Indologist and archaeologist who studied at Presidency University, Kolkata under S. Kuppuswami Sastri. He held posts at the Government Museum in Chennai, the Indian Museum, and the National Museum, New Delhi.

Calvert Watkins was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Harvard University (~1950–1959). He held academic posts at Harvard University (1959–2003) and the University of California, Los Angeles (2003–2013).

Cameron Bailey works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He completed undergraduate studies at Indiana University, earned a master's degree at Florida State University, and studied at Wolfson College, Oxford under doctoral supervisor Ulrike Roesler.

Cameron David Warner specializes in Tibetology and religious studies. He earned a PhD from Harvard University, where he studied under Yudru Tsomu, and held posts at Middlebury College and Dickinson College.
Cameron Kyle Bender Foltz is a scholar in religious studies and Tibetology. He completed an MA at Florida State University under the supervision of Bryan J. Cuevas (attested 2018).

Camillo Alessio Formigatti is an Indologist who studied at the University of Milan. He taught Sanskrit at SOAS, worked on the Sanskrit Manuscripts Project at Cambridge (2011–2014), and served as Sanskrit Librarian at the Bodleian Libraries (attested 2019).

Carl Bielefeldt works in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied under Shunryu Suzuki and earned a PhD from UC Berkeley before serving on the faculty editorial board at Stanford University (~1980–2013).

Carl Cappeller was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Franz Bopp and Albrecht Weber in Berlin, earned a PhD at Leipzig, and completed his Habilitation at Jena, where he became a professor in 1875.
